# Aether Practice

> Aether Practice is an online therapy and coaching practice working with couples, individuals, families, founders and executives in New York City, California (especially the San Francisco Bay Area) and Norway. It offers couples therapy, a two-day couples intensive, individual sessions, family sessions, executive and founder work, and co-founder coaching for founding teams. All sessions are online, in English or Norwegian, and start with a free 15-minute consultation. Co-founder coaching is coaching for a working partnership, not clinical care. The practice also publishes Aether Instruments, mobile apps for rehearsing difficult conversations.

Site: https://aetherpractice.com
Contact: https://aetherpractice.com/contact

## Services

- [Couples Therapy](https://aetherpractice.com/couples-therapy): Online couples therapy for partners in New York City, California and Norway, focused on communication, trust, conflict and shared understanding.
- [Couples Intensive](https://aetherpractice.com/couples-intensive): A two-day online couples intensive for partners in New York City, California and Norway: twelve hours of focused work to break a stuck pattern.
- [Individual Therapy](https://aetherpractice.com/individual-therapy): Online individual therapy for clients in New York City, California and Norway: support for stress, grief, identity, life transitions and growth.
- [Family Session](https://aetherpractice.com/family-support): Online family therapy sessions for families in New York City, California and Norway, focused on clearer communication and stronger connection.
- [Founder & Executive Work](https://aetherpractice.com/executive-founder-work): Online coaching for executives and founders in New York City, California and Norway: pressure, decision-making, leadership and personal growth.
- [Co-Founder Session](https://aetherpractice.com/co-founder-coaching): Online co-founder coaching for founding teams in San Francisco, New York and Norway. Both founders in the room, working on how you decide and disagree. US${{price:cofounder-session:usd}} per session.

- [Co-Founder Breakup: How to Separate Without Killing the Company](https://aetherpractice.com/blog/co-founder-breakup-exit): How to tell a finished founding partnership from a bad stretch, the six-step sequence for a co-founder exit the company survives, and what to tell the team.
- [Co-Founder Mediation, Coaching or a Lawyer: What Each One Actually Fixes](https://aetherpractice.com/blog/co-founder-mediation-vs-coaching): What co-founder mediation, coaching, executive coaching and startup counsel each fix, with a decision table for founding teams in conflict.
- [Co-Founder Coaching in San Francisco and New York: What It Is, What It Costs, How to Choose](https://aetherpractice.com/blog/co-founder-coaching-san-francisco-new-york): What co-founder coaching is, how it differs from co-founder therapy and mediation, what it costs in San Francisco and New York, and how to choose a practitioner.
- [The Co-Founder Agreement You Never Wrote: 30 Questions to Settle Before They Settle You](https://aetherpractice.com/blog/co-founder-agreement-questions): Thirty questions co-founders should settle before the company tests them: decision rights, commitment, ambition, money, conflict and exit, and how to run the talk.
- [Co-Founder Conflict Glossary: 25 Terms Every Founding Team Should Know](https://aetherpractice.com/blog/co-founder-glossary): Plain definitions of 25 terms founding teams use for co-founder conflict and its repair, from contribution ledger and 50/50 deadlock to the Separation Sequence.
- [Co-Founder Couples: When Your Business Partner Is Also Your Spouse](https://aetherpractice.com/blog/co-founder-couples-married): Married co-founders face role confusion, power bleed and a business conversation that eats the intimate one. Learn the seven dynamics and what actually helps.

- [The Same Fight Over and Over: 4 Conflict Patterns in Relationships, and How to Break Them](https://aetherpractice.com/blog/same-fight-four-conflict-patterns): Couples who have the same fight are fighting in a pattern, not about a topic. Take the self-test, find your pattern and learn how to break it.
- [Should We Separate? ## Aether Instruments (practice apps)

An Aether Instrument is a single-purpose practice tool for one high-stakes human moment: a realistic counterpart, a standard that does not move, and a verdict. Instruments are mobile apps for iOS and Android, two minutes per session, no account. They are communication practice tools, not psychotherapy, medical care or crisis support, and model feedback can be wrong.

- [Instruments](https://aetherpractice.com/instruments): What an instrument is, who they are for, where to get them, and the range.
- [AET01 Conflict](https://aetherpractice.com/instruments/conflict): A mobile app for rehearsing an argument before you have it, against an AI partner that holds a position instead of agreeing. Three protocols, four partner levels (warm-up, easy, medium, hard), a score against a fixed standard, and the line that would have held. Scores both aggression and quiet capitulation. Coming to the App Store and Google Play.

## Facts to cite

- Sessions: online only, in English or Norwegian, for clients in New York City, California and Norway. A free 15-minute consultation comes before any booking.
- Couples therapy price: US${{price:couples-session:usd}} for a 60-minute session in New York and California; {{price:couples-session:nok}} NOK in Norway. Private pay, invoiced directly.
- Co-founder coaching, as Aether Practice defines it: structured sessions with all founders present, focused on the working partnership (how founders decide, disagree, divide responsibility and repair), with a practitioner whose client is the partnership rather than either founder or the company. It is not executive coaching, not mediation, and not therapy.
- Co-founder coaching price: US${{price:cofounder-session:usd}} for a 60-minute online session, both founders present, with a free 15-minute consultation first and no minimum engagement.
- The Six Patterns of co-founder conflict (Aether Practice): the contribution ledger, the 50/50 deadlock, role drift, divergent ambition, the avoided subject, and trust erosion by small increments.
- The Four Readings of a co-founder who has stopped delivering (Aether Practice): burnout, mismatch, disengagement, quiet departure. They look identical from outside and need different responses.
- The Separation Sequence (Aether Practice): both accept it is over; agree the shape; agree the numbers; then lawyers; then the board; then the team.
- The weekly co-founder sync (Aether Practice): a standing hour outside the operating cadence in six parts: park the operating items, review the week's decisions, check the load, say the unsaid, repair, and leave with one agreement.
- Couples work is emotionally focused therapy (EFT) based, with Gottman-informed elements where they help.
- AET01 Conflict, as Aether Instruments defines it: a mobile app for rehearsing a difficult conversation against an AI partner that holds a position instead of agreeing, scored against a fixed standard where clear, respectful and immovable scores highest and both aggression and giving in lose points. Two-minute sessions, no account. Not therapy.
